Attached is a concise benchmarking summary (h100_vs_l40s_perf_report.csv). TL;DR: for Bluefin’s profile (avg 350 tokens, mixed short/medium prompts):

- H100 single-GPU throughput: ~95–110 tokens/sec for the target model family at 16–32 seq; p99 latency at target load ~180–240ms depending on batching.
- L40S single-GPU throughput: ~70–85 tokens/sec; p99 latency ~230–320ms under similar batching.
- Performance-per-dollar: assuming committed discounted hourly rates, H100 yields ~1.25–1.35x better tokens/sec per $ than L40S for short-session workloads because of better kernel efficiency at smaller batch sizes.
- Recommendation: Mix pool where 40–50% of reserved capacity is H100 for latency-critical routes, remaining on L40S to improve unit economics. Provide autoscale burst buffer on H100 to absorb peaks (configure burst capacity = +20% for 6-minute window).

Operational notes: routing can pin model variants to hardware class and fallback to L40S variant on capacity shortage. KV cache is isolated per model variant; when falling back your p99 will increase — include a fallback SLA clause. Rolling upgrades are seamless if we keep matching quantization profiles.

I included a short cost table in the CSV — happy to refine numbers with procurement pricing if they share required committed discount band.

—Rishi

Subject: Proposal: 24-mo renewal + 28-GPU reserved pool (mixed H100 / L40S) — draft

Emma / team — attached is a draft proposal and SLA annex for your review (redwood_proposal_24mo_H100_pool.pdf, SLA_Annex_H100_L40S.docx). Key points:

- Term: 24 months (10/01/2026–09/30/2028)
- Reserved pool: 28 GPUs (14 H100, 14 L40S) with pool-level throughput guarantee of 1.25M tokens/sec sustained and burst headroom of +20% for 6-minute windows
- Pricing: blended committed rate with stepped discount: 18% discount on published H100 hourly for first year, 22% year-two; L40S at 15%/18% respectively. Net effect: estimated cost per 1M tokens is ~12% lower vs running all-H100, while preserving p99 latency targets on pinned routes. Detailed table in attached PDF.
- Fallback behavior: if H100 capacity is unavailable, we guarantee a warm-fallback to L40S variant with a defined p99 degradation allowance; full fallbacks will trigger credits per SLA (see Annex).
- Ops: Redwood will provide a migration runbook, pre-warm KV caches for pinned routes at cutover, and one free 4-hour on-call migration window.

Next steps: 1) confirm committed discount band, 2) legal to review SLA Annex, 3) if accepted we’ll send a DocuSign.

Appreciate any quick feedback; we can iterate Friday afternoon on pricing details.

Best,
Aisha
